headline: Computational methods infer cell lineage and fate from single-cell and imaging data
label: Computational Single Cell Lineage Inference
summary: New tools integrate lineage barcodes, transcriptomes, and live imaging to quantify cell fate, state, and division history.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational inference of cell state, lineage, and fate from single-cell and imaging data. Several items couple lineage information with transcriptomes: FateScape integrates lineage barcodes and transcriptomes to infer cell division trees and depth-resolved state patterns, while Cis-TERN integrates scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq via a directed bipartite graph and network diffusion to infer pseudotime. A Bayesian BEAST 2 model handles sparse CRISPR barcode loss without filtering. EpiDiff derives a continuous differentiation index from DNA methylation, and a transformer predicts cancer cell fate from live-cell image sequences. Other items apply the same quantitative logic to imaging: SatelliteQ for centriolar satellites, AnDi-J for single-particle diffusion, and a cell-track method for multicellular pattern formation. What is new is the shift toward open, reproducible workflows and continuous, rather than discrete, readouts of cell state.
